title: ‘Making sure that people are in a good place is draining, and nobody does that for me’: the pandemic and its ongoing impact on teachers and headteachers
abstract: Introduction Due to the Covid−19 pandemic, education provision was significantly disrupted for two academic years. Schools saw an increase in their workload and scope of their responsibilities which impacted staff members physically, mentally and professionally. This study examines how the pandemic and school disruptions impacted teachers and other staff members, and their continued experience since all restrictions have been lifted. Methods Twenty-three staff members were interviewed in the 2021/2022 academic year and nine staff members in the 2023/2024 academic year using semi-structured online interviews. Results Results showed that the pandemic was challenging for staff members with their well-being and workload significantly affected. Even though restrictions in England were lifted in the summer of 2021, staff members are still struggling with the effects of the pandemic, as well as emerging post-pandemic challenges such as the cost-of-living crisis. Discussion Findings from these interviews suggest that the impact of the pandemic has been long-term and highlight the need to include staff members in any discussions regarding recovery plans. title: From information providers to learning designers: heutagogical teaching practices in AI-enhanced education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has intensified longstanding questions about teachers' roles and the pedagogical conditions under which technology supports learner autonomy. This qualitatively driven embedded mixed-methods study examined practices reported and represented by Israeli teachers during an eight-week professional development program on AI, self-regulated learning, and learner-centered pedagogy. The primary qualitative strand drew on reflections, open-ended questionnaire responses, lesson plans, and pedagogical artifacts and used a hybrid deductive-inductive analysis. An exploratory quantitative strand compared 61 consenting pre-program submissions with 26 consenting post-program submissions. Because submissions were anonymous and unlinked, Welch independent-samples tests were used. Post-program means were descriptively higher for reflective teaching, AI-supported planning, and inquiry-oriented design, and essentially unchanged for differentiated instruction; none of the four comparisons was statistically significant after Holm adjustment. title: Exploring primary teachers’ emotional and instructional challenges in supporting students with general reading difficulties in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Introduction This study investigates the instructional and emotional challenges primary school teachers face when teaching students with general reading difficulties in Saudi Arabia. Methods The study employed a descriptive phenomenological design to examine teachers' lived experiences of addressing reading difficulties. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 14 primary school teachers who varied in experience, age, and sex. The data were analyzed using an inductive, data-driven thematic analysis. Results The analysis generated four themes: (a) instructional challenges, (b) emotional and affective challenges, (c) instructional adaptations, and (d) school preparedness and professional develop The findings provide valuable insights into the importance of professional development and educational resources in supporting students with reading difficulties. They also highlight the vital role of primary school teachers in assisting these students and the consequent impact of this responsibility on teachers' workloads. title: Design and exploratory assessment of a mobile educational prototype for Saraguro cultural heritage and Kichwa-language learning
abstract: Introduction Digital resources can broaden access to living heritage, but their contribution depends on cultural relevance, community governance, and claims that remain proportional to the evidence collected. This study reports the design and exploratory assessment of a mobile educational prototype focused on Saraguro cultural heritage and introductory Kichwa-language learning. The prototype organized multimedia content on gastronomy, rituals and festivals, handicrafts, ancestral medicine, stories, cultural places, and basic Kichwa expressions with audio-playback controls. It was informed by a previous project website, saragurotradiciones.site, but the two resources were technically distinct and only the mobile prototype was assessed. Methods The development process was organized through the five Mobile-D phases. An exploratory qualitative evaluation involved 12 purposively selected participants: five undergraduate students, three local tour guides, two cultural-tourism operators, and two educators. title: Teachers' evaluations of evidence— accurate statistical understanding but biased relevance perceptions
abstract: To realize evidence-informed school practice, teachers need to critically evaluate scientific findings, drawing on, among other factors, their attitudes and their educational research literacy. However, evaluating such findings is a complex process that can be distorted by different cognitive biases, such as anchoring effects. Preliminary research has shown that some aspects of teachers' evaluation of research are heavily biased, while others are quite accurate. Against this backdrop, this study aims to investigate the extent to which anchoring effects shape different components of teachers' evaluations of evidence. Based on dual-process theories, relevance perceptions might be influenced by intuitive processing (System 1), which is why we hypothesize that willingness-to-pay ratings as a proxy for relevance perceptions are susceptible to anchoring effects. In contrast, effect magnitude estimates might be formed by deliberate reasoning processes (System 2) and thus remain unaffected. title: Data collection and analysis for neurodevelopmental disorders: a single-case study and tutorial for clinicians and educators
abstract: It is generally acknowledged that optimizing teaching and learning is best accomplished with real-time data and rapid analysis and feedback. This is perhaps especially true for individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders whose highly individualized learning profiles make standardized approaches insufficient. However, for the vast majority of such individuals, practical limitations limit the accomplishment of this ideal. Here, we present a fully implemented approach to data-driven interventions, developed and tested in a home-based, full-time hybrid clinical-educational program for an individual with autism (level 3). The system encourages real-time data recording with minimum interference with ongoing activities, and a data analysis and reporting pipeline grounded on freely available software that does not require extensive statistical knowledge. This system could potentially be a base for others to build on and modify for specific situations and needs.

title: Influence of AI tools across research processes on the research productivity of postgraduate students in Nigerian public universities
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming research practices in higher education, yet empirical evidence on how AI supports research productivity among students remains limited, particularly in developing contexts. This study examined the influence of AI tools used during the research preparation, analysis, and dissemination stages on the research productivity of postgraduate students in public universities in Nigeria. The study was guided by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) and Experiential Learning Theory. Methods The study adopted a descriptive survey design involving 312 respondents. Data were collected using the AI Tools Utilisation and Research Productivity Questionnaire (AITURPQ) and analysed using simple linear regression. The analysis examined the predictive effects of AI-assisted research preparation, analytical, and dissemination tools on research productivity. Results The findings reveal that AI-assisted research preparation tools significantly predicted research productivity (R² = .241, p < .05). title: A framework for authentic assessment in legal and ethical business curricula
abstract: Introduction Legal and Ethical Business (LEB) curricula in higher education (HE) are traditionally taught through lectures and subsequently assessed via invigilated examinations. These methods have been shown to result in suboptimal student engagement, with challenges to students inculcating the desired theoretical knowledge. Studies have shown that authentic assessment (AA) offers a viable alternative towards enhancement of student learning, engagement, and skill development while maintaining academic integrity. This study proposes an authentic assessment practical framework for LEB. The proposed framework may support the adoption of AA in LEB curricula and in turn have a positive impact on student learning in higher education. Methods A systematic literature review (SLR) was employed to identify, evaluate, and synthesise existing research on the topic. The review followed a structured search, screening and categorisation process to develop the proposed evidence-informed framework for AA. title: A methodology for AI-supported cross-level professional collaboration in computer science education using the AI-Ustaz platform
abstract: Introduction Contemporary educational environments require educators to participate in professional networks that extend across institutional levels. This study presents a methodology for AI-supported cross-level professional collaboration involving pre-service teachers, secondary-school teachers, and college instructors, with the AI-Ustaz platform serving as the shared technological environment. Methods The methodology comprised three sequential stages: theoretical–orientational, technological, and project–networked. A cluster quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was implemented during the 2024–2025 academic year with 347 participants across nine educational institutions in Kazakhstan. Participants were allocated to an experimental group (n = 178) and a control group (n = 169). Cognitive, performative, and reflective components of networked-collaboration competence were assessed. Results Descriptive analyses indicated greater pretest-to-posttest improvements in the experimental group across the cognitive, performative, and reflective components. title: Generative AI as a catalyst for critical thinking: reframing students from consumers to co-creators
abstract: This study examined students’ AI literacy, perceived learning benefits, and ethical awareness following participation in a structured, AI-integrated classroom activity. The study also investigated the relationships among these constructs and examined whether perceived learning benefits mediate the relationship between AI literacy and ethical awareness. In addition, the study explored whether students’ responses differed according to gender, prior AI experience, and frequency of AI use. The study involved 104 undergraduate students who participated in a hands-on classroom activity over two academic semesters. Students used generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, to prepare and deliver short lessons to their classmates, followed by discussions addressing responsible and ethical AI use. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring AI literacy, perceived learning benefits, ethical awareness, and related aspects of students’ experiences. title: From journal validation to quality governance: a policy analysis of India's transition from UGC-CARE to quality-oriented research assessment and its implications for medical and dental education
abstract: Background The University Grants Commission (UGC) announced the discontinuation of the UGC-CARE Reference List through a Public Notice dated 11 February 2025, following the Commission's decision taken at its 584th meeting on 3 October 2024, marking a major shift in India's approach to research quality governance. Introduced in 2019 to address predatory publishing, the UGC-CARE framework provided a centralized mechanism for identifying credible publication venues. The transition to quality-oriented research assessment emphasizing publication ethics, peer review integrity, editorial transparency, and institutional accountability has generated considerable debate, yet its implications for research integrity and health professions education remain insufficiently explored. Methods A narrative policy analysis was conducted using publicly available UGC policy documents, regulatory reports, international responsible research assessment frameworks, and peer reviewed literature. title: Not all body percussion is equal: alignment and temporal cue weight in second language phonology
abstract: Body percussion, the intentional production of sound through clapping, patting, stamping, and snapping, is among the most widely used embodied techniques in language classrooms; however, no theoretical account specifies how a rhythmic bodily action might become a phonological representation available for speech production. This study addresses this gap. title: An NLP-assisted and explainable rule-based platform for formative feedback from academic similarity reports
abstract: Introduction Academic similarity reports identify textual overlap but do not, by themselves, determine plagiarism or explain how students should revise their writing. This study describes an implemented, explainable, teacher-mediated workflow and reports a preliminary feasibility-oriented assessment of teacher-perceived usefulness. Methods The platform processed information from 200 real, deidentified undergraduate similarity-report cases from a single institution. Fifteen instructors reviewed editable feedback drafts through a web interface and selected Accept, Review, or Redo, mapped analytically to Correct, Partial, or Adjust. Case-level exploratory analyses examined associations between teacher ratings and recorded severity, operational issue category, source type, similarity percentage, and number of sources. Results Correct, Partial, and Adjust ratings were recorded for 65 (32.5%), 75 (37.5%), and 60 (30.0%) cases, respectively. title: Family cultural capital and academic achievement in a smaller-city Chinese high-school context: evidence from Linfen
abstract: Purpose Family cultural capital is an established explanation of educational inequality, and its relationship with academic achievement has been examined in previous Chinese research. Rather than proposing a new cultural-capital construct, this study provides an extension by examining the relative associations of cultural resources, parental education level and parent-child communication with academic achievement among high school students in Linfen, Shanxi Province. Methodology The study focuses on a smaller-city educational setting that has received less attention than national datasets and major metropolitan contexts in the literature considered here. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was administered to 200 students aged 16–18 from two high schools in Linfen, Shanxi Province, selected through stratified cluster sampling. Academic achievement was measured using students’ reported end-of-term performance across three municipal examination subjects. title: What is a green school? Understanding stewardship, well-being, and sustainability education
abstract: This research article examines the notion of the green school through the lens of health and wellness; outdoors education; and stewardship of resources. The article first overviews the framework of the U.S. Department of Education Green Ribbon Schools (ED-GRS) recognition which includes the three green pillars of reducing environmental impacts , areas of facilities, transportation, grounds and operations; improving health and wellness through coordinated school health, with consideration to air quality, learning environment, school nutrition, and outdoors physical activity; and offering effective environmental and sustainability education that emphasizes hands-on, real-world learning, civic engagement, and STEM. We provide a brief descriptive analysis of the 769 ED-GRS award recipients over a 13 year period that spans 585 schools, 123 districts, and 60 postsecondary institutions. Our analysis yields insights on potential gaps that have emerged in practice. title: Rebuilding through science: a hybrid STEMM recovery model for higher education reconstruction in Gaza
abstract: This review examines the role of science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and medicine (STEMM) education in the long-term reconstruction of Gaza following the extensive destruction of its higher education system since 2023. Evidence is drawn from institutional assessments, peer-reviewed research on higher education in Gaza, and comparative studies of other conflict-affected systems, including Syria, Afghanistan, Ukraine, and Sudan. Quantitative indicators are drawn from four source families employing methodologically distinct procedures, namely satellite and field-based damage assessment, an interim damage assessment applying rapid damage and needs assessment methodology, national statistical survey, and administrative casualty records reported by the Palestinian Ministry of Education and Higher Education, with points of divergence, single-source indicators, and remaining verification limits reported explicitly. abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by students to obtain explanations, generate ideas, improve written responses and prepare assessment tasks. However, limited evidence exists on how students in open-distance alternative-access programmes experience GenAI in mathematics assessment. Methods This qualitative study examined how 27 Higher Certificate students at a South African open and distance learning institution described the role, benefits and limitations of GenAI while preparing fraction-related portfolio activities. Data were collected via a single open-ended questionnaire item, completed voluntarily after all assessment activities had been submitted. The responses were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Four overlapping themes were identified: support for understanding and approaching tasks, support for constructing written responses, conditional trust and evaluative engagement, and non-use, resistance and ambiguous engagement. title: Interactive effects of supervisory styles and institutional contexts on the practical innovation ability of professional degree postgraduates
abstract: Introduction As the global knowledge economy increasingly demands high-level applied talents, cultivating practical innovation ability has become a priority for professional degree postgraduate education. Drawing on the Componential Theory of Creativity and Resource Dependence Theory, this study conceptualized practical innovation ability as a multidimensional construct integrating innovation knowledge, skills, thinking, disposition, and performance. Methods Using survey data from 3,338 professional degree postgraduates across 20 Chinese universities, this study employed two-way analyses of variance to examine how supervisory styles interacted with university level and university type in shaping practical innovation ability. Results The results revealed significant interactions between supervisory styles and institutional characteristics. title: Perceived educational value, ethical risk, and support for responsible AI governance in higher education: an embedded mixed-methods study
abstract: Introduction Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is becoming increasingly embedded in higher education assessment, yet the perceptual factors that motivate stakeholder support for its institutional governance remain underexamined. This study investigated the extent to which Perceived Educational Value (PEV) and AI Ethical Risk Perception (AERP) are associated with Responsible AI Governance Support (RAGS) among higher education stakeholders. Methods An embedded mixed-methods survey design was employed. Quantitative Likert-scale data and qualitative open-ended responses were collected concurrently through one structured questionnaire; full-sample quantitative analyses were conducted first, followed by thematic analysis of the open-ended responses to contextualize and deepen interpretation of the quantitative findings. title: The B-AIMT: development and initial validation of a domain-specific instrument for assessing mathematics teachers’ beliefs about artificial intelligence
abstract: This study presents the development of the Belief Scale for Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics Teaching (B-AIMT) and provides psychometric evidence for its initial validation as a domain-specific instrument assessing teachers’ beliefs about AI in mathematics instruction. Based on data from 442 German pre-service and in-service teachers, confirmatory factor analyses provided support for a theoretically grounded multidimensional belief structure comprising nine latent belief dimensions organized within two overarching domains: beliefs about student mathematics learning with AI and beliefs about mathematics teaching with AI. The resulting subdimensions capture perceived instructional affordances, epistemic potentials, perceived risks, and ethical considerations related to AI systems. The final measurement model showed satisfactory model fit and good internal consistency. title: Teaching coherence and cohesion to Chinese EFL undergraduates: a concept-based classroom intervention
abstract: Despite the importance of coherence and cohesion to effective writing, few studies have examined how these concepts can function as a psychological tool for thinking and writing. To advance this line of inquiry, we presented a mixed-methods research that employed the Concept-based Language Instruction (C-BLI) to teach coherence and cohesion to Chinese English as Foreign Language (EFL) learners, with an aim to examine changes in learners' conceptual understandings and writing performance following the intervention. Data sources included written texts, metalinguistic knowledge tests as well as learning process data from four focal students. Quantitative pretest-posttest comparisons revealed substantial improvements in learners' conceptual understanding, whereas no statistically significant changes were observed in overall writing quality or coherence and cohesion. title: School leadership mentoring across four European educational contexts: an exploratory qualitative study
abstract: Over the past decades, school leadership has become a central element in educational reform, school improvement, and organizational effectiveness across education systems worldwide. Nevertheless, European education systems continue to reflect diverse governance arrangements shaped by national trajectories and institutional legacies. Although school leadership is widely recognized as a key determinant of educational effectiveness, comparatively limited research has examined how mentoring for school leaders is configured within distinct governance contexts. Addressing this gap, this study undertakes an analysis of six leadership trajectories from four European countries selected for their contrasting governance orientations: Portugal and Spain as cases reflecting traditions that tend to be more centralized, and Belgium and the Netherlands as cases characterized by a tendency toward greater decentralization and stronger school-level autonomy. title: Concrete reading theory: embodied anchors for early literacy in digital contexts
abstract: Background Foundational literacy models have long privileged visual–auditory decoding pathways, systematically marginalising the haptic, proprioceptive, and affective systems that evolutionarily predate symbolic processing. The accelerating digital transformation of early childhood has compounded this problem by replacing hands-on, material engagement with screen-mediated interaction, raising urgent questions about the sensorimotor foundations of orthographic learning. Social belonging and academic mindset affect student performance in an introductory biology course at a two-year college
abstract: Introduction Access-oriented institutions serve increasingly diverse student populations and play an important role in broadening participation in STEM. However, relatively little research has studied how affective factors contribute to student success in introductory STEM courses, specifically Introductory Biology, within these settings. This study examined how the affective constructs of social belonging (sense of belonging and belonging uncertainty) and academic mindset (entity and incremental beliefs) relate to student performance in Introductory Biology at a U.S. two-year institution. Methods Survey and exam data were collected across 16 course sections ( N = 310). Theory-driven hierarchical and multiple regressions models, controlling for academic preparation, were used to examine relationships among affective variables and performance. Because these affective variables are underexplored in these contexts, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted and supported the expected two-factor structures for both measures. title: Scientific and methodological foundations for teaching physicochemical analysis methods in continuous chemical education: a scoping review
abstract: Background Rapid technological advancement, digitalization of analytical instrumentation, and the growing demand for interdisciplinary competence have significantly transformed the role of analytical chemistry in science and industry. These changes necessitate a systematic reconsideration of how physicochemical analysis methods are taught within continuous chemical education. Objective This scoping review aimed to map and systematize the structural components of modern analytical chemistry education, identify dominant pedagogical approaches, and conceptualize their functional interrelationships within an integrated educational framework. Design/methods The study was conducted as a scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search was performed in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ACS Publications, SpringerLink, and RSCI (eLIBRARY.ru), covering publications from 1975 (the earliest eligible record retrieved) to 2024. Eligible studies addressed pedagogical, curricular, or methodological aspects of teaching analytical chemistry or physicochemical analysis methods. title: AI-TPACK readiness and generative AI integration among mathematics lecturers in Ghana's public colleges of education: predictors of AI-TPACK readiness
abstract: Despite growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) in education, empirical evidence on AI-extended Technological Pedagogical and Content Knowledge (AI-TPACK) readiness and generative AI integration among mathematics lecturers remains limited, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined AI-TPACK readiness and generative AI integration among mathematics lecturers in Ghana's public Colleges of Education and investigated whether AI literacy, self-efficacy in AI use, and teaching experience predicted AI-TPACK readiness. A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 214 mathematics lecturers from 49 public Colleges of Education in Ghana. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring AI-TPACK readiness, generative AI integration practices, AI literacy, self-efficacy in AI use, and teaching experience. Descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression were used to analyse the data. The findings showed that overall AI-TPACK readiness was moderate (M = 2.48, SD = 0.71). title: Do you prefer UDL? Bridging the gap between students and faculty in the implementation of universal design for learning in higher education
abstract: The consolidation of inclusive education in higher education has driven the adoption of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) as a framework for promoting more accessible, flexible, and equitable environments. However, questions remain regarding the degree of alignment between the inclusive strategies implemented by faculty and student preferences. The objective of this study was to conduct a comparative analysis of university students’ preferences and faculty members’ reported application of teaching strategies based on UDL. A quantitative, cross-sectional, non-experimental, and comparative study was conducted. A total of 196 participants took part (170 students and 26 faculty members). A structured questionnaire on effective strategies for inclusive higher education aligned with the UDL was used, consisting of 37 items grouped into six dimensions. The instrument demonstrated adequate levels of internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from.78 to.89 for students and from.72 to.85 for faculty members. title: Design and evaluation of a novel digital teaching and learning process for higher education: a proof-of-concept study
abstract: Introduction Digital transformation in higher education has increased the demand for instructional approaches that promote learner engagement, inclusivity, information literacy, and self-directed learning. Although microlearning, Universal Design for Learning (UDL), and constructive alignment have individually demonstrated educational benefits, limited research has explored their integration within a unified pedagogical framework. This study designed and evaluated a novel digital teaching and learning process that integrates microlearning, connective alignment, and the principles of UDL to enhance teaching and learning in higher education. Methods To evaluate the impact of the novel digital teaching and learning process, a case study was conducted in the “Evidence-Based Practice in Physiotherapy” course in the BSc in Physiotherapy curriculum. A mixed-methods proof-of-concept study employing a randomized crossover design was conducted to evaluate the academic effectiveness, the students’ perceptions of the teaching, and the students’ satisfaction. title: Human-written and AI-generated revisions: an appraisal analysis of dialogic positioning in argumentative writing
abstract: Introduction This study presents a systematic comparative analysis of appraisal resource use across human-written and AI-generated texts. Drawing on Appraisal Theory, with a focus on Engagement, it compares first drafts, peer-feedback revisions, and AI-generated revisions, which were produced by ChatGPT-4 based on students’ first drafts using a standardized prompt. Method To conduct the comparison, a corpus of 168 essays across the three draft types was compiled based on four writing tasks completed by undergraduate English majors in China. All drafts were manually coded and data were analyzed using linear mixed models and descriptive statistics. title: Gender differences in attitudes toward disability among university students in health and education programs
abstract: Introduction Positive attitudes toward disability are essential for promoting inclusive educational and healthcare practices. However, evidence remains inconclusive regarding how gender, academic discipline, and previous contact with people with disabilities shape these attitudes among university students. The aim of this study was to examine whether attitudes toward disability differ according to gender, degree program, and previous contact with people with disabilities among university students enrolled in health and education degrees. A secondary aim was to explore whether the factors underlying favourable attitudes differ by gender using classification tree analysis. Methods A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted involving 446 university students from Extremadura, pursuing degrees in Physical Activity and Sport Science, Occupational Therapy, and Early Childhood Education, participated in this comparative research. title: Impact of virtual and hands-on laboratory experimentation on the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge: a meta-analysis
abstract: Introduction Hands-on laboratory experimentation is an important contributor to the successful acquisition of conceptual science knowledge, but its practical application has several limitations. Virtual laboratory experiments help overcome most of these shortcomings and may also be more effective than hands-on laboratory activities in promoting conceptual science knowledge acquisition. Methods In this study, the impact of virtual and hands-on laboratory experimentation on the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge was compared by means of a meta-analysis. The meta-analysis encompassed 43 studies selected according to the predefined inclusion criteria, and the principles of Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses procedure. For each study, one effect size value of Hedges' g was calculated. Subsequently, due to their heterogeneity, the overall effect size value was computed through the use of the random-effects model. title: Peer review contributions as a measure of academic distinction requirements of faculty promotion committees: rapid review of top-ranking universities
abstract: Introduction Journal peer review expertise is a cornerstone of academic practice. However, research publication productivity often overshadows prepublication peer review as a marker of academic distinction. The objective of this review is to examine the status of peer review contributions as a criterion of academic performance within faculty promotion committees at leading universities. Methods We reviewed handbooks, guidelines, and procedures related to faculty promotion and tenure on the official websites of the top 50 universities ranked by the QS World University Rankings 2025. Peer review, as a requirement of academic promotion, was identified and reported if it fell within the scope of, a) peer review reporting or authoring, b) peer review education or mentoring, or c) peer review training or learning. The primary assessment criteria governing academic promotion were reported. title: Collaboration as an effective tool for the implementation of the Lesotho inclusive education policy 2018: opportunities and challenges
abstract: Background The implementation of the Lesotho Inclusive Education Policy 2018 is complex and requires a collaborative approach. Given the complexity of inclusive education, the paper acknowledges that there must be participation of different role players in helping teachers to effectively carry the mandate of the policy. Aims The study aims to explore how collaboration is effective in supporting the education of Learners with Special Education Needs (LSEN) through the perspectives and experiences of teachers and provides a comprehensive evidence-based approaches for improving the implementation of inclusive education policies through a collaborative approach. Methods The paper is framed within ecological systems theory to understand how collaboration as premised on the LIEP 2018 could effectively help the implementation phase of the policy. The paper is lensed under the interpretive paradigm and designed with a qualitative research approach. Nine teachers were purposively selected from a regular school and were engaged in a focus group discussion. title: Active pedagogical approaches in physical education across school and higher-education contexts and in physical education teacher education: a systematic review of pedagogical models, outcomes and implementation conditions (2005–2025)
abstract: Background Physical Education (PE) and Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) increasingly use student-centred pedagogical approaches, but evidence from learner-oriented PE contexts and professional teacher education is often synthesised together. This systematic review examined active pedagogical approaches in PE and PETE between 2005 and 2025, focusing on pedagogical models, learner and professional outcomes, and implementation conditions. Methods Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, ERIC, SPORTDiscus and PubMed in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Three reviewers independently conducted study selection, data extraction and MMAT appraisal, resolving discrepancies by consensus. The protocol was not prospectively registered. Owing to substantial contextual and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively rather than meta-analytically. Results The final synthesis included 141 studies: 30 PETE, 37 university PE/higher education, 29 secondary PE, 21 primary PE, 23 mixed school-university/PETE-school, and one school-unspecified study. title: Making mathematical reasoning visible: a qualitative comparative case study of students’ reasoning, representation, and communication
abstract: Developing students’ capacity for mathematical reasoning and communication is a central goal of contemporary mathematics education, yet qualitative evidence on how these competencies are externalized during problem solving remains limited. This study investigates how students’ mathematical reasoning, use of representations, and modes of engagement differ in the ways 19 they become visible during problem solving, even when solutions are mathematically correct. Adopting a qualitative comparative case study design, three secondary school students exhibiting contrasting modes of engagement were examined while solving a non-routine algebraic problem designed to elicit representational transitions and justification. Data were drawn from written solution artefacts and follow-up semi-structured, artifact-based interviews. Thematic analysis focused on reasoning documentation, representational coordination, and forms of mathematical communication, emphasizing processes of externalization rather than evaluative correctness. title: Transformation of the teaching role through educational automation and intelligent technologies: a systematic review
abstract: Introduction Educational automation is increasingly used in teaching, but its implications for teachers' tasks, responsibilities, and professional agency remain insufficiently synthesised across educational levels. This review examined how automated and intelligent technologies are transforming the teaching role. Methods Empirical studies indexed in Scopus and Web of Science from 2020 to 2024 were reviewed following PRISMA 2020. Eligibility was structured using PICO, and methodological quality was appraised with the 2018 Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Results Fifty-eight studies met the eligibility and quality threshold: 41 quantitative, eight qualitative, and nine mixed-methods studies. Three domains emerged: teachers' adoption perspectives and constraints; technology-mediated models that redistribute teaching work; and educational outcomes conditioned by teacher competence, institutional support, and governance. Twenty-four studies met five MMAT criteria, 20 met four, and 14 met three. title: iSTEAM and TLIF as frameworks for artistic and mathematical creativity: a comparative conceptual review
abstract: This article offers a comparative conceptual review of the innovative Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (iSTEAM), and Teaching and Learning Inquiry Framework (TLIF) as two distinct yet complementary pedagogical frameworks for fostering mathematical and artistic creativity. It starts from the premise that creativity in education cannot be adequately understood unless it is examined simultaneously through pedagogical, psychological, philosophical, and aesthetic perspectives. Using an integrative review design, the paper synthesizes empirical studies, theoretical works, and review literature published mainly between 2015 and 2025, with selected earlier sources included to trace the historical development of key concepts. The analysis argues that iSTEAM and TLIF share a common foundation in modern and late-modern educational thought, drawing on inquiry, constructivism, symbolic representation, and reflective judgment. title: Patterns of geometric problem-solving errors among pre-tertiary students across levels of geometric reasoning
abstract: This study examined pre-tertiary students’ geometric problem-solving performance, the distribution of their errors across Van Hiele levels of geometric reasoning, and the nature of these errors using Newman's Error Hierarchical Model. A descriptive quantitative research design, complemented by qualitative content analysis of students’ written responses, was adopted. The sample comprised 300 final-year students selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-designed Geometry Problem-Solving Test consisting of twelve open-ended items aligned with the senior high school geometry curriculum. Students’ responses were analysed using frequency and percentage distributions, while error patterns were classified using Newman's framework and mapped onto Van Hiele levels. The findings showed generally low performance in geometry problem solving, with most students scoring within the lower performance range. title: A multilevel living lab using a digital-twin-based modelling environment for sustainability education and decision support
abstract: Sustainability education increasingly requires learning environments that connect systems understanding with real-world decision-making. This study examines the integration of a district-heating digital-twin-based modelling environment into a multilevel living-lab process at Riga Technical University, Latvia. An exploratory mixed-method case study was conducted over 13 months and involved 24 professionals in the co-creation stage, 196 undergraduate students working in 98 pairs, 30 master's students working in 15 pairs, and eight external stakeholders. Data included World Café outputs, 294 undergraduate scenario responses, modelling-environment simulation outputs, master's student multi-criteria decision analyses, and stakeholder evaluations. Quantitative scenario outputs were examined in relation to emissions, costs, and system performance, while participant-produced materials were analysed to identify patterns in systems reasoning, trade-off recognition, and decision priorities. title: Student teachers' perceptions of conditions for reflection in digital supervision
abstract: Introduction Reflection constitutes a central component of the knowledge base of the teaching profession; however, in practice it may become routinized and have limited significance for professional learning. Within teacher education, supervision increasingly takes place in digital contexts, raising questions about the conditions required for such supervision to support reflection. In this study, we examine which conditions student teachers describe as significant for reflective processes in digital supervision. Methods The study is based on six focus group interviews with a total of 36 student teachers. The data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The design gives access to how student teachers perceive these conditions, not to reflection as it unfolded in individual supervision sessions. The theoretical framework draws on e-mentoring as an analytical perspective for understanding how relational, communicative, and technological conditions interact in technology-mediated supervision. title: Metacognitive thinking and academic self-regulation as predictors of academic burnout among university students in Jordan
abstract: Background This study examined the predictive relationship between metacognitive thinking, academic self-regulation sub-dimensions, and academic burnout among undergraduate students in Jordan. Methods Using a convenience sample of 631 students, three validated scales were administered: the Metacognitive Awareness Inventory, the Academic Self-Regulation Inventory, and the Academic Burnout Inventory. Two-way ANOVA, correlation analyses, and multiple stepwise linear regression were employed to analyze the data. Results Two-way ANOVA revealed no statistically significant differences in metacognitive thinking, self-regulation, or academic burnout based on gender. However, significant differences were identified based on the year of study; upperclassmen (third- and fourth-year students) demonstrated significantly higher levels of metacognitive thinking and self-regulation, whereas first-year students reported the highest levels of academic burnout. title: Transforming intensive reading instruction: a four-method pedagogical framework for enhancing reading proficiency in higher education
abstract: The reading-to-pedagogy gap in universities and universities of education reveals the necessity for integrated approaches in the understanding instruction in higher education. In this study, the Four-Method Pedagogical Framework (4MPF) incorporating metacognitive strategy training, morphological awareness training, collaborative dialogic reading, and technology-instructive adaptive feedback was researched. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was used, with a 12-week randomized controlled intervention with 147 undergraduate students, and further qualitative inquiry to clarify and clarify the quantitative results. The 4MPF yielded significantly higher reading comprehension gains than traditional instruction ( p < .001; Cohen's d = 0.82). Partial statistical mediation was confirmed as there were significant indirect effects via metacognitive regulation and morphological awareness, and a significant direct effect was perceived. A qualitative analysis resulted in four explanatory themes: cognitive empowerment, lexical confidence, dialogic friction, and feedback dependency. title: Bridging barriers through technology integration in mathematics education: a qualitative multiple-case study of rural schools
abstract: Introduction This study explores how barriers to technology integration in mathematics education can be bridged within rural and resource-constrained school contexts. Although technology is increasingly recognised as a catalyst for improving access, equity, conceptual understanding, and learner engagement, meaningful ICT integration remains limited in many under-resourced schools due to persistent structural and pedagogical barriers. Guided by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, the study contributes to the literature by examining how teachers employ contextually responsive strategies to integrate digital technologies in mathematics classrooms. Methods This qualitative multiple-case study explored mathematics teachers’ experiences and perceptions of technology integration across three rural secondary schools in the Vhembe District, South Africa. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews with six mathematics teachers and three Departmental Heads. title: Teachers’ use of generative artificial intelligence in K–12 education: a systematic review
abstract: Background The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has created new opportunities and challenges for teachers, leading to a growing body of research on its educational applications. AI has become increasingly integrated into instructional processes, supporting teachers in tasks such as lesson planning, assessment, feedback generation, content creation, and classroom support. Despite the rapidly increasing number of studies on AI in education, the literature on teachers’ use of GenAI is distributed across different contexts, methodologies, and theoretical perspectives. Therefore, this systematic review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of research on teachers’ use of GenAI in Pre-12 and K-12 education. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies were screened and selected based upon the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 79 empirical studies included in the final analysis. title: Measuring attitudes of ethical use of GenAI in the work of university educators in Slovakia
abstract: Existing AI ethics frameworks provide broad principles for responsible AI use in higher education. However, empirical evidence remains limited on how university educators prioritize and differentiate concrete ethical dilemmas arising across their academic work. Within the literature included in a preceding systematic literature review, no study empirically examined the complete set of 31 identified ethical problems across seven domains of university educators' academic activity. This cross-sectional quantitative survey therefore investigated educators’ attitudes toward these problems and established their relative priorities for institutional AI governance. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 388 educators at Slovak public and private universities using a faculty-stratified recruitment strategy. Responses were analyzed using two-tailed one-sample t -tests against the scale midpoint, Cohen's d, repeated-measures ANOVA, and Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons. title: Phenomenological framing in teacher noticing research: how theoretical perspectives constitute their objects
abstract: Teacher noticing has become one of the most generative yet contested constructs in teacher education research. Cognitive, sociocultural, and ecological-embodied perspectives are often discussed as alternative, and sometimes potentially complementary, accounts of teacher noticing. This paper advances a stronger meta-theoretical account: through their framing operations, these perspectives can constitute distinct research objects rather than merely illuminate different aspects of a common one. Building on an earlier formulation of phenomenological framing, I systematize the concept as the constitutive work through which a theoretical perspective determines where noticing is located, what standards define its adequacy, and how it is organized in time, thereby shaping what counts as evidence and what remains theoretically less visible. title: The competence enactment paradox: teacher innovation as the missing mechanism in the DIPTERA model of professional development
abstract: Introduction Digital competence frameworks and digital-pedagogy orientations may be associated with teachers' continuing professional development (CPD), but the statistical pathways linking them remain under-specified. This study evaluated the theory-informed DIPTERA model (Digital Innovation-mediated Professional Transformation through Enacted Readiness Architecture), which specifies Teacher Innovation (TI) as a statistical mediator and Teacher Digital Readiness (TDR) as a downstream outcome in the tested model. Methods A cross-sectional design was used. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was applied to self-report responses from 554 vocational high-school teachers in Indonesia. title: A STEM-based learning trajectory for developing spatial reasoning in 8-year-old children: online and face-to-face implementations
abstract: We present a STEM-based learning trajectory, centered on the phenomenon of earthquakes, that aims to develop spatial reasoning in eight-year-old children. The trajectory has as an end product the design of an evacuation route. Based on a framework integrating spatial reasoning actions, reference frames, and the differentiation of micro-, meso- and macrospaces, the trajectory tasks combine concrete resources (measuring tools, recycled materials) with digital ones (e.g., Google Maps, Google Earth, LightBot) so that students can analyze representations, measure distances, as well as construct and test instruments and artifacts (e.g., a seismograph) not usually included in the primary school curriculum. It is designed to help students articulate and move between different spatial sizes and their representations and use adequate measuring instruments for each. Within a design-based research (DBR) study, the trajectory was implemented with groups of children from a disadvantaged context in Mexico, in two phases and in different modalities: online, during the Covid-19 pandemic, and face-to-face the following year. title: Associations of metacognition, self-directed learning ability, and AI literacy with academic achievement among university students predominantly enrolled in health-related majors: a cross-sectional study
abstract: The expanding integration of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has heightened the need to identify learner competencies associated with academic achievement. This study examined the associations of metacognition, self-directed learning ability, and AI literacy with self-reported academic achievement among university students in the Republic of Korea. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted with 175 undergraduates from 11 universities between September 30 and November 1, 2025; 78.3% were enrolled in health-related majors. Metacognition, self-directed learning ability, and AI literacy were measured using the SMI, SDLI, and MAILS, respectively; academic achievement was measured as self-reported cumulative GPA on a 4.5-point scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, Pearson correlations, and hierarchical multiple regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors. title: A proof-of-concept EEG study of responses to peer speech in collaborative learning
abstract: Background This study focused on internal aspects, including cognitive states and motivational engagement, that may be overlooked by external indicators of participation in collaborative learning, such as utterance counts or observable behaviors. This proof-of-concept feasibility study explored whether neurophysiological responses related to auditory attention could provide information relevant to interpreting conventional behavioral indicators of participation. Using electroencephalogram (EEG) indices (N1 and P2 components), associations with self-regulated learning and interest during collaborative learning were explored. Methods EEG data were collected during real, discussion-based collaborative learning activities conducted in a university classroom setting. EEG data were recorded using wearable devices from nine Japanese university students enrolled in the course. title: Integrating immersive VR into STEM-based physics teaching: student perspectives on the Rutherford experiment simulation
abstract: Introduction Teaching complex and abstract concepts in atomic physics remains challenging. Integrating STEM principles, applied-oriented learning, and immersive technologies such as virtual reality (VR) may support conceptual understanding and visualization. Methods This study combined bibliometric analysis, a quantitative meta-analysis of 15 eligible empirical studies, and a pilot VR-based assessment. The pilot involved 22 pre-service physics teachers who completed a VR-based lesson on Rutherford's experiment and evaluated the learning experience using a Likert-scale survey covering conceptual clarity, visualization and interactivity, motivation and interest, and STEM and applied orientation. Results The meta-analysis showed a strong positive effect of STEM- and applied-oriented instruction on learning outcomes, with a mean standardized difference (Cohen's d) of 1.28 (95% CI: 0.98–1.58). The pilot assessment also showed generally positive student evaluations across all four dimensions. title: Core university functions as predictors of university teachers’ digital competence
abstract: Introduction The digital transformation of higher education has redefined the professional profile of university teachers, positioning digital competence as a key component of educational quality and innovation. In this context, the study aimed to analyze the predictive effects of digital competence in research, outreach, and management on digital competence in university teaching at the Technical University of Manabí and the State University of Milagro. Methods A quantitative, explanatory approach was adopted, with a non-experimental cross-sectional design. The sample consisted of 315 teachers from both universities. A structured questionnaire with high reliability ( α > 0.98) was used. Digital competence in university teaching was specified a priori as the endogenous criterion construct and was therefore not entered as an exogenous predictor; digital competence in research, outreach, and management were modeled as the three predictor constructs. Structural equation modeling was applied using SPSS and AMOS to estimate the magnitude and direction of the relationships. title: Bringing virtual reality-integrated social-emotional learning into schools: a dual-phase validation and feasibility study with adolescents in a collectivist society
abstract: Social-emotional learning (SEL) is increasingly recognised as an important approach to adolescent mental health promotion in school settings. However, evidence regarding culturally adapted and technology-supported SEL interventions in non-Western educational contexts remains limited. This study reports the expert-validation and pilot-feasibility components of the REAL™ (Read Emotion and Learn to Regulate) module, a culturally adapted, virtual reality (VR)-integrated SEL intervention developed for Malaysian lower-secondary students. These developmental phases preceded a subsequently completed and separately reported randomised controlled trial (RCT). A sequential two-phase design was used. In Phase 1, six Malaysian experts from psychiatry, psychology, education, and social-emotional learning completed a three-round Modified Delphi process evaluating 15 module structure and delivery components and 12 activity stations on a 5-point Likert scale. title: The impact of artificial intelligence on the quality of legal education in the UAE: a critical analysis of legal, pedagogical, and ethical considerations
abstract: The adequate application of artificial intelligence (AI) technology in legal education in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has been barely covered by scholarly literature, especially, from the perspectives of legal and educational sciences. The current paper attempts to fill in an existing gap in literature about the appropriate usage of AI in legal education. The research is intended to help curriculum designers in UAE universities to improve undergraduate legal education programs using innovative AI systems and, thus, to provide UAE policy makers with the academic and ethical standards for the use of AI in legal education. The current paper critically discusses the possible contribution of AI systems in the improvement of the quality of legal education. Moreover, the research analyzes the probable implications of using AI in law curricula for the learning process and for the development of critical legal skills in UAE law students, stressing on the importance of ensuring academic integrity. title: Refining teachers’ ethical knowledge in smart learning environments - a Delphi study within the TPCEK framework
abstract: Smart Learning Environments (SLEs) increasingly integrate artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies, creating new ethical demands for teachers’ professional knowledge. This study employed a three-round Delphi design to refine the definitions and conceptual boundaries of eight predefined ethics-related dimensions of the Technological Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (TPCEK) framework for preservice preschool teachers in SLEs. Twenty experts evaluated the dimensions in terms of necessity, definitional clarity, contextual appropriateness, and conceptual distinctiveness. Quantitative evaluations were integrated with qualitative feedback to guide iterative refinement. All eight dimensions met the predefined necessity criterion. Round 1 identified conceptual ambiguity primarily in Content Ethical Knowledge, Technological Pedagogical Ethical Knowledge, Technological Content Ethical Knowledge (TCEK), and Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (PCEK). title: The reality of identifying gifted children in Qatar from the perspective of early childhood teachers: a mixed-methods study
abstract: Introduction This study examined early childhood education professionals' perceptions and lived experiences regarding the identification of gifted children in Qatar. Methods An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed. In the quantitative phase, 226 teachers and coordinators completed a 20-item questionnaire, and the associations between overall perceptions and demographic and professional variables (job title, years of experience, school type, highest academic qualification, and prior training) were examined. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight early childhood teachers, and the data were analyzed thematically to explain and deepen the quantitative findings. Results Overall perceptions were high (M = 3.83, SD = 0.37), with strong endorsement of creativity as a central component of giftedness and support for the feasibility of early identification. title: A real-time multimodal attention monitoring system for online learning: integrating behavioral, affective, and activity indicators to support adaptive teaching
abstract: Introduction The fast growth of online and hybrid learning has increased the need for effective tools to monitor student attention during virtual lectures. Existing systems often depend on one or two models and do not combine behavioral, affective, and activity cues within a single structure. Methods This paper proposes a browser-based intelligent system to support adaptive teaching that refers to adjusting instruction according to students' attention levels .The proposed system integrates four complementary AI models for real-time attention monitoring without needing software installation. title: Engineering a sustainable future: the impact of service-learning on technical knowledge and civic responsibility in STEM higher education
abstract: Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) calls for higher education institutions (HEIs) to equip graduates with the competencies needed to address complex sustainability challenges while fulfilling their Third Mission of community engagement and societal development. This study presents a small, exploratory, one-group pretest-post-test pilot evaluation of the EDUSTEM framework, a service-learning approach designed to integrate sustainability-oriented learning into STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) education through interdisciplinary, community-based learning experiences. An exploratory mixed-methods design without a control or comparison group was employed with 50 undergraduate STEM students and pre-service teachers enrolled at the largest technical university in Southeastern Europe. Curriculum analysis informed the co-design of service-learning modules with faculty members and community stakeholders. The programme was evaluated using pre- and post-intervention surveys, competency assessment rubrics, and thematic analysis of students’ reflective journals. title: Cognitive empathy and psychological distress in health sciences students: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction Cognitive empathy, understood as the ability to adopt another person's perspective, is a key socioemotional competence in health professions education and has been associated with psychological adjustment and lower levels of psychological distress. However, evidence on how cognitive empathy and psychological distress vary across disciplines and stages of training remains limited, particularly in large multidisciplinary samples. The present study aimed to (1) analyze differences in cognitive empathy and psychological distress across Health Sciences degree programs and stages of training and (2) examine the relationship between cognitive empathy and psychological distress while controlling for relevant sociodemographic and academic variables. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 1,754 undergraduate students enrolled in Medicine, Nursing, Physiotherapy, Psychology, and Human Nutrition and Dietetics at a Spanish university. title: What does educational inclusion mean in theory and practice for learners with severe and profound learning disabilities?
abstract: This paper is a dialogue between two experts in the field of the education of children and young people with severe and profound learning disabilities (SLD/PMLD) who address the question: What does educational inclusion mean in theory and practice for learners with severe and profound learning disabilities? The dialogue illustrates how concepts reflect a dynamic interaction between value positions and conceptual framing. Peter Imray argues that curricula for all do not work for all. He argues that even strong differentiation of the same curricula does not serve learners with SLD/PMLD well. title: Reconfiguring graphic design education for generative AI in higher education: a human-agency and adaptive-curriculum framework
abstract: Introduction Generative AI creates a curriculum-transformation problem by redistributing activities through which disciplinary expertise is learned, practised, demonstrated, and assessed. This study examines that problem within graphic design education as a bounded empirical case. Methods A survey of 270 participants was analysed using exploratory factor analysis ( N = 265 complete cases), and semi-structured interviews with 12 design academics and practitioners were analysed using a frozen rule-based codebook across 650 meaning units. The quantitative and qualitative strands were analysed independently and integrated through a joint display. Results The quantitative analysis yielded a broad, sample-specific Transformative–Normative response orientation and a narrower Curricular Diagnostic Critique cluster; neither is interpreted as a validated latent construct. title: Improving young learners’ language practice and engagement through the BalaTalk digital platform
abstract: Introduction Young learners require repeated exposure, active participation, and sufficient time-on-task to develop vocabulary and oral language competence in Kazakh and Russian. Traditional primary classrooms, however, may not provide every pupil with frequent vocabulary repetition, immediate feedback, and equal opportunities for oral participation. This study examined the short-term effectiveness of the BalaTalk digital learning platform as a supplementary tool for language practice among third-grade pupils in Kazakhstan. Methods A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group design was employed with 75 pupils from six intact classes across three schools. The intervention lasted one school week. Pupils in the experimental group used BalaTalk for 15-20 minutes per day during regular lessons, whereas pupils in the control group received traditional instruction without the platform. title: Empirical studies on the development of music therapy training programs
abstract: This study examined experiential educational interventions for music therapy training in Japan, where opportunities for clinical practicum are limited. To address this educational challenge, simulated music therapy sessions were used as a controlled approximation of clinical interactions, although they cannot fully reproduce the complexity of real clinical practice. Two experiential approaches were investigated: physical imitation, in which participants reproduced a partner's movements, and eye closure, in which participants closed their eyes while listening to and interacting with the partner. The interventions were designed to engage different aspects of clinical listening, including attention to partners’ behaviors and sounds, emotional and intentional interpretation, and awareness of interpersonal interaction. Seventy-six undergraduate music students participated in a 2 × 2 factorial design examining physical imitation (present vs. absent) and eye closure (present vs. absent). title: Project-based learning technologies and the professional preparation of special education teachers in Kazakhstan
abstract: This study examines how project-based learning technologies contribute to the professional preparation of future special education teachers in Kazakhstan. A quantitative-supported qualitative research design was employed. The participants consisted of 76 undergraduate students and 11 professors from the History and Pedagogy/Special Pedagogy department at Uzbekali Zhanibekov South Kazakhstan Pedagogical University, selected through convenience sampling. Data were collected through a researcher-developed form including descriptive survey items and open-ended questions. Descriptive data were analyzed using frequencies and percentages, while qualitative responses were analyzed through content analysis. The findings showed that both students and professors conceptualized project-based learning as a practice-oriented approach that connects theoretical knowledge with real pedagogical situations. title: Traditional and modern education systems in Ayurveda education: a critical integrative review
abstract: The evolution of Āyurveda education reflects a shift from an ancient, philosophically grounded educational model to a contemporary, institutionalized, competency-based one. Historically, Āyurveda was transmitted through the Gurukul system, a personalized, residential pedagogical model combining textual study with hands-on clinical training, emphasizing moral discipline ( Dharma ) and the Guru-Śiṣya Paramparā (teacher-disciple lineage). Learning was structured around the Trividha Jñānopāya (three-fold means of knowledge) and the cognitive sequence of Śravaṇa (listening), Manana (reflection), and Nididhyāsana (internalization). Colonial administrative frameworks and subsequent modernization transitioned Āyurveda education into a structured, time-bound, standardized university system. title: Factors associated with Chinese vocational college students’ intention to use generative artificial intelligence for learning: an extended UTAUT mode
abstract: This study focuses on examining the factors influencing Chinese vocational college students’ behavioral intention to use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for learning and further analyzing the relationships between these factors and changes in GenAI behavioral Intention. Based on the Unified Theory of behavioral Intention and Use of Technology (UTAUT), an extended model incorporating anxiety (ANX) was developed, and a two-stage analytical approach combining structural equation modeling (SEM) and ordered Probit (OProbit) regression was adopted. In the first stage, SEM was employed to examine the effects of various factors on behavioral intention within the extended UTAUT model. In the second stage, an OProbit model was applied, with changes in GenAI behavioral Intention specified as an ordinal outcome variable, to further examine the relationships between the relevant factors and changes in behavioral Intention while controlling for individual characteristics, including gender, grade level, and prior AI usage experience. title: Strategic leadership for agentic AI in education: a conceptual framework with reference to the United Arab Emirates
abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) shifts educational leadership from whether to adopt a tool to which actions a configured system may take, under whose authority, and with what capacity for intervention and remedy. Through critical integrative synthesis of educational leadership, organisational decision-making, AI governance, and agentic-AI scholarship, this Conceptual Analysis develops educational agentic alignment: a relational judgement about whether delegated machine authority fits educational purposes, human decision rights, professional capabilities, safeguards, pedagogy, and public-value obligations. The focal unit is a dated and versioned educational delegation arrangement. The framework separates agentic capability, use-related exposure, and usable governance capacity; organises leadership decisions through seven domains across four levels; and proposes three mechanisms concerning safeguard shortfall, responsibility–capacity mismatch, and evidence-linked realignment. title: Artificial intelligence in university physics education: a systematic review of empirical studies
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into higher education, yet empirical evidence on its pedagogical use in university physics remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesized empirical research on the applications, reported learning and pedagogical outcomes, methodological quality, challenges, and educational implications of AI-supported university physics education. We used six search sources: SpringerLink, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and ERIC. The searches in the five original sources were updated through September 2026, and ERIC was added as an additional search source. Eligibility criteria were defined using the PICOS framework, study selection followed PRISMA 2020, and methodological quality was appraised using the 2018 Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Eleven empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were synthesized narratively. Across the included studies, AI was used for tutoring and explanations, formative feedback and scaffolding, collaborative problem solving, simulation and modeling, instructional design, and developing AI literacy. title: Technology integration in basic school mathematics instruction: exploring teachers’ perceptions, readiness, and challenges
abstract: Despite growing recognition of technology as a catalyst for improving mathematics teaching and learning, its integration in basic school classrooms remains inconsistent, particularly in developing contexts where teachers often face pedagogical and contextual constraints. This study examined basic school teachers’ perceptions of technology incorporation in mathematics instruction, assessed their readiness for technology integration, and explored the challenges influencing its implementation. The study adopted an explanatory sequential mixed-method design involving 150 basic school mathematics teachers selected through stratified random sampling for the quantitative phase and five purposively selected teachers for the qualitative phase. Data were collected using an adapted structured questionnaire and a semi-structured interview guide. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics in SPSS (Version 27), while qualitative data were analysed thematically. title: Prompt-Mediated Curriculum Development: a human–AI co-design framework for AI-mediated curriculum development in higher education
abstract: The integration of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education is transforming curriculum development by enabling AI systems to contribute to the design of learning outcomes, assessments, instructional activities, and other curriculum artefacts. Despite growing interest in AI literacy, prompt engineering, and human–AI collaboration, limited attention has been given to how educators enact curriculum expertise within AI-mediated design environments. This conceptual paper introduces the Prompt-Mediated Curriculum Development (PMCD) framework, which conceptualises curriculum development as an iterative process of human–AI co-design mediated through prompt literacy. Drawing on curriculum theory, sociocultural perspectives on mediation, human–AI collaboration, and AI literacy scholarship, the framework positions prompt literacy as the central mechanism linking educator expertise, agentic AI systems, and curriculum artefacts. Prompt literacy is defined as the ability to formulate, refine, and evaluate prompts in ways that support pedagogically aligned and contextually relevant educational outcomes. title: Multilingual academic publishing in Kazakhstan: language shifts during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This study aims to examine changes in the distribution of Kazakh-, Russian-, and English-language publications during and after the COVID-19 pandemic using the Eurasian Journal of Philology: Science and Education as a case study. The corpus comprises 535 articles published in Kazakh, Russian, and English between 2020 and 2025, including 278 articles from the pandemic period (2020–2022) and 257 from the post-pandemic period (2023–2025). The corpus was analysed using quantitative methods, keyword analysis, and scientometric techniques. Publication patterns were compared across the periods 2020–2022 and 2023–2025, with particular attention to the interplay between language choice, thematic focus, and the journal's disciplinary sections, including linguistics, literary studies, language teaching methodology, and translation studies. The findings reveal a statistically significant shift in the distribution of publication languages between the pandemic and post-pandemic periods, although the magnitude of the association was small. title: The future of virtual business education: students’ continuance intention in Colombian business schools
abstract: Colombian business schools are experiencing a transformation characterized by changing enrollment patterns, declining participation in some traditional face-to-face programs, and continued growth in virtual education. Drawing on a post-adoption perspective informed by the Expectation-Confirmation Model and the perceived-usefulness mechanism of the Technology Acceptance Model, this study examines the relationships of satisfaction, perceived usefulness, and perceived quality with students' continuance intention toward virtual classes. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 807 students enrolled in business-related programs at 12 private accredited universities in Bogotá, Colombia. Data were collected online between July 2024 and September 2025 using a non-probability sampling strategy combining convenience and snowball procedures. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Satisfaction was the strongest predictor of continuance intention to use virtual classes ( β = 0.54, p < 0.001; f 2 = 0.29), followed by perceived usefulness ( β = 0.23, p < 0.001; f 2 = 0.08). title: Educommunication and artificial intelligence for learning, creating, and communicating: professional competency development in university prosumers
abstract: Introduction This study examines the pedagogical integration of educommunication and artificial intelligence (AI) and its association with self-reported professional competencies among university prosumers-students who simultaneously consume, produce, and share academic content through digital platforms. Methods A non-experimental, cross-sectional quantitative design with descriptive-correlational and structural purposes was employed. Data were collected using a psychometrically validated 26-item Likert-scale questionnaire (plus six open-response items) administered to a convenience sample of 547 university students enrolled at Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, Ecuador. The instrument assessed five dimensions: (1) AI-mediated learning processes, (2) educommunication and expression, (3) knowledge prosumption, (4) perceived professional competencies, and (5) ethics and critical AI use. Psychometric validation confirmed excellent reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.91; McDonald's ω = 0.93).
